Represent a phylogeny by one vector related to a predictor

Source: R/phylo_gradient.R
phylo_vector.Rd

The phylogenetic representation of Peres-Neto et al. (2012). Eigenvectors of the phylogenetic distances are extracted with species weights. A global test relates all of them to the predictor. Only if it is significant, eigenvectors enter in the order of their correlations until the first that is not significant, and they are summed with their correlations as weights (pev). Brownian vectors are then added to pev, and the sum with the largest correlation is kept (pev_brown).

Usage

phylo_vector(
  comm,
  tree,
  env = NULL,
  n_perm = 999,
  level = 0.05,
  n_sim = 1000,
  site_permutations = NULL,
  alpha = NULL,
  predictor = NULL
)

Arguments

comm

Matrix with one row per site and one column per species. Every site needs at least one individual. Or an mc_data() object, whose parts fill the arguments left out.

tree

A phylo object.

env

Numeric vector with the value of each site. The authors estimate one vector for each predictor.

n_perm

Number of permutations of sites and of species.

level

Significance level of the global test and of the selection.

n_sim

Number of Brownian vectors.

site_permutations

Optional matrix of site indices with one permutation per row, for example from torus_permutations(), to use instead of free permutations. Empty sites are then allowed: they leave the analysis but their values can reach occupied sites.

alpha

Deprecated, use level.

predictor

Deprecated, use env.

Value

List of class mc_phylo_vector with correlation, the correlations of pev and pev_brown; p_site, p_species and p_max of the global test; selected, the columns of eigenvectors retained; pev and pev_brown, named vectors or NULL when the global test is not significant or no eigenvector is retained; eigenvectors; eigenvalues; eigenvector_correlation; and permutations. Check pev before combining gradients with cbind(), which drops a NULL without warning.

Details

The correlations are fourth-corner correlations, and the p-value to report is the larger of the tests that permute sites and species (ter Braak et al. 2012). For a test between a trait and the environment, see ade4::fourthcorner(). The two vectors are chosen to fit the predictor, so a further test of them is not valid on its own. They are meant for trait_partition() after a significant global test.

Species are matched to the tips of tree by name, in any order, and those in only one of the two are dropped with a warning. Species without individuals have no weight and are left out.

Note

Adapted from the MATLAB functions TraitEnvCor, ModelSelectionStochastic and PCoAWeigthed in the supplement of Peres-Neto et al. (2012).

Article and original code

The functions TraitEnvCor, ModelSelectionStochastic and PCoAWeigthed and the script ScriptDemo of the supplement differ from the article and its appendices in the points below. Here we follow the text, except in the addition of Brownian vectors and where noted.

  • Weights of the eigenvectors: the text uses the correlations and the code their absolute values, so eigenvectors with opposite signs cancel.

  • Brownian vectors: the text multiplies each one by pev and the code adds them. We follow the code, as the product of a random vector with mean zero would not keep the structure of pev.

  • Number of Brownian vectors: 1000 in the text and 100 in the code.

  • Distances: the text uses the square root of the path length, and the script one minus the covariance.

  • Centring: Q in the text only centres if the weights sum to one, and the script passes the sums of the species. PCoAWeigthed also does not divide the coordinates by the square root of the weights. DoubleCenterWeigth, which the script does not call, does both and agrees with this function.

  • Global test: the text regresses each eigenvector on all predictors, and the code accepts one. With one predictor both are the same statistic. We also take one predictor.

  • Forward selection: the text tests each eigenvector given the remaining predictors, and the code tests its simple correlation. We follow the code.

  • Significance level: Appendix B uses 0.05, and the code uses alpha / 2 for every permutation strategy, although Appendix A gives alpha / 2 only for the stacked test. Here the larger p-value is compared with level.

  • p-value of the global test with row permutations: the code divides by twice the number of permutations, which halves it.

  • No significant result: the code returns random normal vectors, which can then enter later analyses. Here pev and pev_brown are NULL.

  • Choice of vector: the article recommends the one with the highest R2, and the script always takes the Brownian vector. Here both are returned.

  • Combination of permutations: Appendix A stacks the two null distributions, adds one to the count and uses alpha / 2, and TraitEnvCor adds two. The stacked p-value is close to the mean of the two p-values, so any test that it rejects at alpha / 2 is also rejected by the larger p-value at alpha, which we use.

  • Permuted variables: Appendix A recalculates the statistic, and TraitEnvCor keeps the observed mean and standard deviation, so a permuted variable no longer has weighted mean zero. Here it is standardised again, as in the code of the partition.

  • The code runs n_perm - 1 permutations in each null distribution.

  • The supplement calls eigen, which it does not include, and the example 2 of ScriptDemo removes rows of PhyloDistance before creating it.

References

Peres-Neto, P. R., Leibold, M. A., & Dray, S. (2012). Assessing the effects of spatial contingency and environmental filtering on metacommunity phylogenetics. Ecology, 93, S14–S30. doi:10.1890/11-0494.1

ter Braak, C. J. F., Cormont, A., & Dray, S. (2012). Improved testing of species traits–environment relationships in the fourth-corner problem. Ecology, 93, 1525–1526. doi:10.1890/12-0126.1

See also

Other environment and space: plot_trait_partition(), trait_partition()

Examples

set.seed(1)
tree <- treeshapesim::sim_tree_shape(20)
traits <- species_traits(tree, lambda = 1, optima_range = c(0, 100),
                         rmax_range = c(0, 30))
env <- runif(50, 0, 100)
comm <- simulate_static(traits, env, incidence = TRUE)$abundance
keep <- rowSums(comm) > 0
phylo_vector(comm[keep, ], tree, env[keep], n_perm = 99, n_sim = 100)
#> <mc_phylo_vector> 18 eigenvectors, 2 retained
#> permutations: 99 free of sites, 99 of species; smallest possible p: 0.01
#> global test: p (sites): 0.01  p (species): 0.01  p (max): 0.01 
#> correlation: PEV 0.61  PEV-B -0.595
